candidate.title: HiTS-RAP
candidate.scope: The HiTS-RAP row of the assigned Illumina poster: preparation and sequencing of RNA-encoding DNA clusters, regeneration of double-stranded templates, Tus/Ter-dependent T7 transcription halting, labeled-protein binding and flowcell scanning. This is the Tus/T7 implementation clarified by Tome et al. (2014), with corroborating Ozer et al. (2015) protocol evidence. Neighboring TRIBE, TRAP-Seq, partial RBNS labels and the right-side chemical legend are separate poster context, not alternatives or branches of this assigned row. The RNA display is the binding substrate; the sequenced library is DNA, and the final depicted readout is fluorescence, not a new RNA-derived sequencing library.

states.label: Protein-binding fluorescence at flowcell cluster coordinates
features: Cluster-associated fluorescence is intended to report protein binding to displayed RNA. The primary paper matches these intensities with d1 by cluster coordinates; that downstream matching is explained here rather than drawn as an additional operation.

A concentration series, reported in the primary paper but compressed to one bind/scan pair in this diagram, supports affinity estimation; a single image alone does not determine a dissociation constant.
Fluorescence can also contain contributions from protein binding to DNA, Tus or T7 RNA polymerase; the display does not by itself guarantee RNA-specific binding.
Surface immobilization can affect apparent affinity. The depicted implementation measures equilibrium binding affinity, not binding on- and off-rates or endogenous RNA occupancy.

evidence.quote: These data were then matched by cluster coordinates to their sequence from .qseq.txt files generated by the Illumina OLB version 1.9.4.
It was then equilibrated successively with increasing concentrations of mOrange labeled protein in binding buffer and imaged.
Application of HiTS-RAP to proteins that interact with DNA, T7 RNA polymerase, or Tus protein would be complicated, as these interactions will contribute to the observed protein binding.
HiTS-RAP is susceptible to steric hindrance effects especially for large proteins due to surface immobilization of RNAs.
As presented, HiTS-RAP does not measure binding kinetics (on- and off-rates), but measures binding affinity (Kd).

operations.label: Transcribe and halt

operations.label: Scan flowcell

checks.rationale: Independent review supports acceptance at the declared HiTS-RAP schematic/Tus-T7 implementation scope. All seven operations, twelve states and eighteen routes have been checked individually against the image and relevant primary text. The library is RNA-encoding DNA, the binding substrate is RNA retained through halted T7 polymerase, and the readout is protein fluorescence linked to the earlier DNA sequence by cluster coordinates. Flowcell attachment and the Tus/polymerase scaffold persist through binding and inspection. Joint inputs represent actual hybridization or association; o1 legitimately produces a material and sequence data. No independent molecular branches are collapsed. Scope and every supplied reference are assessed at their actual evidence levels. No consequential unsupported claim, omitted in-scope transformation, incompatible interface, or source discrepancy requiring correction remains.
